correctness.rationale: For every positive m, parity forces odd m, and m=1 fails. For an odd prime power the finite reciprocal geometric sum is strictly below 3/2. With two distinct primes p<q and p>=5 the abundancy is strictly below (5/4)(7/6)=35/24, so p=3. Writing T=3^(a+1), exact multiplication by q-1 gives (T-q)(q^b-1)=4(q-1); thus T-q is a positive integer equal to 4/(1+q+...+q^(b-1)). For b>=2 this is less than 1; b=1 gives q=T-4. Conversely (T-1)(q+1)=Tq+3 when q=T-4, and the prime cofactor is >=5. This proves the unrestricted classification by distinct support, independently of the cutoff. The independently checked large q=10460353199 has no trial divisor through 102275; the corresponding m=36472996363223648799 satisfies the exact identity and 102461 divides (m-1)/2. The frozen VERIFICATION.md lines 23–29 report the 1,000,000 sieve, three hits and 367461 eligible integers; verify.py lines 23–66 implement it. That recorded sieve was inspected, not run or taken as the universal proof. The original expert, independent-audit, and Lean fields were not_performed.

value.rationale: An exact natural low-support boundary for an established Diophantine equation replaces a list of examples and a sufficient family with a full characterization at arbitrary exponents. The composite-neighbor witness concretely separates the standalone question from the older adjacent-pair construction.
